feedback.Dismiss: ACCURATE ANALYSIS: Correctly dismissed legitimate ETL batch synchronization. You verified the files were standard .parquet data tables on the analytics_export share, the process was the authorized etl_sync.exe binary under service account 'svc_etl_batch', and no ransomware indicators (like shadow copy deletion) were present.

educational_rationale.topic: High-Volume File Operations: Ransomware vs Business ETL Ingestion
educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Security+ SY0-701 (Section 4.2 Triage Heuristics, Section 3.1 Operational Baselines) & Network+ (Section 4.1 SMB File Sharing & Port 445)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: High file modification rates on SMB (port 445) trigger behavioral threshold alerts. To distinguish between ransomware and batch ETL jobs: (1) Share Name: Ransomware accesses ADMIN$ or C$ to drop remote stubs; ETL jobs access designated business shares like \\*\analytics_export; (2) File Extensions: Ransomware introduces random or ransom extensions (.locked, .enc) and drops ransom note .txt files; ETL jobs manipulate valid business formats (.parquet, .csv); (3) System Recovery: Ransomware executes vssadmin to destroy restore points; ETL jobs never touch vssadmin or wbadmin.
